evidence.source: Museum of the Institute of History & Philology, Academia Sinica
evidence.field: 甲骨文释形与卜辞用例
evidence.text: The museum interprets oracle-bone 年 as 禾 above 人, depicting a person bearing grain, and cites the paired charge “我受年 / 我不其受年” as asking whether there would be a good harvest. This documents a Shang harvest use; it does not establish that this is the character’s first use.
evidence.kind: institutional paleographic account with transcribed inscription
evidence.title: 我受年──甲骨文「年」的故事

evidence.text: The supplied rows give 人 = rén and 年 = nián. These are current Mandarin readings and do not establish an ancient phonetic relationship. The official character-specific Unicode record pages were attempted but could not be inspected.
evidence.kind: local structured reading rows; upstream verification failed
evidence.title: Unihan Data Lookup (U+4EBA; U+5E74)

evidence.source: Local structured historical phonology supplied in research input
evidence.field: sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, exact 人 and 年 rows
evidence.text: The supplied Baxter–Sagart 2014 rows give 人 OC *ni[ŋ], MC nyin, and 年 OC *C.nˤi[ŋ], MC nen. The notation is preserved as supplied. This historical comparison is relevant to evaluating a proposed sound role but does not by itself establish that 人 functioned phonetically in the earliest 年 graph; no external page for these exact rows was inspected.
evidence.title: Baxter–Sagart 2014 table rows (local dataset)

search_audit.query: 年 oracle bone 受年 harvest earliest attestation Academia Sinica museum
search_audit.outcome: Opened the Academia Sinica museum account and verified its interpretation of 年 and the Shang “我受年 / 我不其受年” inscription. Attempted both official Unihan character pages; both were inaccessible through the browser. Supplied local kMandarin rows were used as local data, not as externally verified Unicode records.

gaps: The museum evidence supports an early Shang harvest use, not the claim that 年 first meant harvest or that this is its earliest attested use overall.

The official Unicode character-specific records for 人 (U+4EBA) and 年 (U+5E74) could not be inspected. Current readings rén and nián are available only from the supplied local Unihan rows; Baxter–Sagart readings are likewise supplied local data, not externally verified pages.
The current-reading pair and supplied historical reconstructions do not settle whether 人 had a phonetic role in the earliest 年 graph.
